name: Aardwolf Loot Tracker
author: Solao
description: Records what drops from what, shop stock and room resources, and parses every id box that scrolls past.
script:
--[[
    aw-loot.lua
    Sean Stoves (Solao) — 2026-08-05

    Loot Tracker. Every item you take off a corpse is recorded with the mob it
    came from and the room you were in. Shop stock and room resources go in
    their own tables, and any identify or appraise box that scrolls past is
    parsed for stats — so appraising something in a shop fills the database
    with no extra traffic and nothing to remember.

    Ported from the Mudlet loottracker, which was itself a port of the
    MUSHclient one. What changed for this client, and why:

    STORAGE. Mudlet had a real db: layer over SQLite. This client has none —
    saveTable is a JSON blob keyed by name, and that is the whole of it. Your
    own captures are small enough to hold whole, but item_stats grows with the
    shared pool and a single blob of every item on Aardwolf would be decoded at
    every startup. 5.5MB of Lua in the libs folder already wedged this client
    once. So item_stats is sharded by first letter and a bucket is only read
    when something in it is wanted; a resident index of names makes search
    possible without loading any of them.

    HTTP. Mudlet's error event carried no status, so a dead key and a bad
    minute looked identical and the sync had to fail three times before daring
    to re-register. Here the callback gets (status, body, error), so a 401 is
    a 401 and nothing else re-auths.

    COLOUR. selectString/getFgColor became parseAnsiText, same as the shop
    panel.

    TAGS. Core sends 'tags on' and gags the protocol noise. A gagged line still
    reaches every trigger, so the {invdata} block is read here while Core keeps
    it off the screen — no hand-off between the two, unlike Mudlet where both
    calling deleteLine on one line ate the line after it.
]]

plugin = {
    id          = "aw-loot",
    name        = "Aardwolf Loot Tracker",
    version     = "1.13.6",
    author      = "Solao",
    description = "Records what drops from what, shop stock and room resources, and parses every id box that scrolls past.",
    settings    = { saveState = true },
}

--[[
    Drop every handler already on a widget event.

    Looked up through _G rather than called by name: a global this build does
    not have throws on the way IN, before pcall can catch anything, so a bare
    reference would take the plugin down on any client that lacks it.
]]
local function drop_handlers(id, event)
    local ok, fn = pcall(function() return _G["unregisterWidgetEvent"] end)
    if ok and type(fn) == "function" then pcall(fn, id, event) end
end


-- @category utilities

local TAG  = "$Y[Loot v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w "
local TAGR = "$R[Loot v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w "

local API_URL = "https://api.aardwolf.muds.fyi"

--[[
    Per-world, which is the default scope.

    Not "global": that is one namespace shared by every character on every
    world, and what drops from an Aardwolf mob has no business being visible
    on a different MUD. The default store is that world's file — isolated
    between worlds, and shared by every plugin and session on the same one, so
    a search that ties players, mobs and drops together still reads all of it
    by name without any of those plugins being loaded.
]]
local SCOPE = nil

--[[
    Upload in slices capped by BYTES, not row count. The MUSHclient version
    learned that a ~144KB body never arrived — past roughly one socket buffer
    fewer bytes reach the wire than content-length advertises. A row cap alone
    wouldn't do it either: one item with a long notes field can blow the budget
    on its own.
]]
local MAX_BODY   = 32768
local FULL_EVERY = 7 * 86400        -- re-declare the whole database weekly

local APPRAISE_MAX, APPRAISE_WAIT = 60, 1000

--[[
    A partial box is re-read this often at most. Without the identify wish
    every 'id' comes back partial, so full_id never reaches 1 and a
    "skip what's already done" check alone never fires — the same item would be
    identified again on every drop, forever.
]]
local REID_AFTER = 7 * 86400

--[[
    Hester's Whoswhatzit, Aylor. Standing here, 'identify' returns the full box
    without the wish — for a fee scaled to the item's level.

    A vnum rather than a room name, because names are decorated and translated
    and this one is a fact.
]]
local HESTER = 32611

local cfg = {
    idwish   = false,   -- do you have the identify wish?
    autoid   = false,   -- identify drops automatically; wants the wish
    idnote   = true,
    inv      = true,    -- send invdata beside 'inv' so containers are learned
    bags     = "bag,backpack,pouch,sack,satchel,purse,quiver,holding,pack,wallet,keyring",
    flags    = "godly,divine,mythical,fabled,epic,legendary,eternal,exalted,"
            .. "majestic,wondrous,radiant,brilliant,dazzling,shimmering,gleaming,"
            .. "sparkling,vibrant,shiny,burnished,enhanced,polished",
    authkey  = "",
    authname = "",
    lastfull = 0,
}

---
-- small helpers
---

local function trim(s)
    return (string.gsub(tostring(s or ""), "^%s*(.-)%s*$", "%1"))
end

--[[
    A field as text, or "".

    Named as_text rather than txt. The short name resolved to nothing inside
    the pool-sync callback — 'Can't find variable: txt' — while being defined
    at chunk scope and present in the built payload, ahead of every use. Three
    ReferenceErrors tonight were names that plainly existed, so rather than
    keep guessing at why a two-letter-plus-one name goes missing in one
    closure, it now has a name nothing is likely to be shadowing.

    NOT 'x or ""'. A field a record doesn't have reads back as undefined after
    a save/load round trip, and undefined is truthy — so the or never fires and
    the line prints "Weapon: undefined". A potion has no weapon_type, no
    inflicts and no dam_type, so an appraised potion printed garbage on every
    row it didn't have.
]]
local function as_text(v)
    if type(v) == "string" then return v end
    return ""
end

-- the same, with a stand-in for the empty case
local function shown(v, dash)
    local t = as_text(v)
    if t == "" then return dash or "?" end
    return t
end

--[[
    An item name in the colour the MUD painted it.

    item_color has always been captured and never used — every listing printed
    in the same white. $X takes a 24-bit hex foreground, so the stored colour
    goes straight back out with no schema change and no palette to map onto.

    Rows migrated from MUSHclient store an @-coded string here instead of a
    hex; those are left plain rather than printed as literal @ codes.
]]
local function paint(name, colour)
    name = as_text(name)
    local hex = string.match(as_text(colour), "^#(%x%x%x%x%x%x)$")
    if not hex then return name end
    return "$X" .. hex .. name .. "$w"
end

--[[
    Every word has to appear, in any order, anywhere.

    'optical precision' finds "[Potion] Optical Precision" and so does
    'precision optical'; 'breakfast' finds "[Pill] Neophyte Breakfast". Plain
    substring matching only did the last of those, which is how searching for
    an item you were looking at came back empty.

    Split by hand: %s is a Lua class and these patterns run on a JavaScript
    regex engine.
]]
local function fuzzy(hay, term)
    hay = low(as_text(hay))
    term = low(trim(term))
    if term == "" then return true end

    local word, any = "", false

    for i = 1, string.len(term) + 1 do
        local c = (i <= string.len(term)) and string.sub(term, i, i) or " "

        if c == " " then
            if word ~= "" then
                any = true
                if not string.find(hay, word, 1, true) then return false end
                word = ""
            end
        else
            word = word .. c
        end
    end

    return any
end

local function amount(v)
    local n = tonumber(v)
    if type(n) ~= "number" then return 0 end

    --[[
        NaN is a number as far as type() is concerned, and tonumber(undefined)
        gives you one. It then poisons everything it touches: the stat count
        read back as NaN, every increment kept it NaN, and the panel rendered
        'with full stats  NaN'.

        x ~= x is true only for NaN.
    ]]
    if n ~= n then return 0 end

    return n
end

local function low(s)
    return string.lower(tostring(s or ""))
end

local function now()
    return os.time()
end

-- walked, not gsub-looped: that loop ends on gsub's replacement count and this
-- runtime transpiles to JavaScript. Written the idiomatic way it spins forever.
local function commas(n)
    n = tonumber(n)
    if type(n) ~= "number" then return "0" end

    local s, out, c = tostring(math.floor(n)), "", 0
    for i = string.len(s), 1, -1 do
        out = string.sub(s, i, i) .. out
        c = c + 1
        if c % 3 == 0 and i > 1 then out = "," .. out end
    end
    return out
end

--[[
    Read capture n from a trigger callback.

    The guide says captures[1] is the first group; our own S&D hedges at
    captures[0] because arrays crossing the Lua/JS boundary arrive 0-indexed.
    The wildcards table is keyed by the STRING "1" and has no index base to get
    wrong, so it goes first.
]]
local function cap(c, w, n)
    if type(w) == "table" and type(w[tostring(n)]) == "string" then
        return w[tostring(n)]
    end
    if type(c) == "table" then
        if type(c[n]) == "string" then return c[n] end
        if type(c[n - 1]) == "string" then return c[n - 1] end
    end
    return ""
end

local function csv_set(s)
    local t = {}
    for word in string.gmatch(tostring(s or ""), "[^,]+") do
        local w = low(trim(word))
        if w ~= "" then t[w] = true end
    end
    return t
end

local function set_csv(t)
    local a = {}
    for w in pairs(t) do table.insert(a, w) end
    table.sort(a)
    return table.concat(a, ",")
end

local exclude     = csv_set(cfg.bags)
local bonus_flags = csv_set(cfg.flags)

---
-- colour
--
-- Aardwolf paints item names and the colour carries meaning: the bonus-loot
-- bracket tier, and whether something is quest or clan gear. Read it off the
-- line rather than deciding for ourselves what an item should look like.
---

local function segments(raw)
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then return nil end
    local ok, segs = pcall(parseAnsiText, raw)
    if not ok or type(segs) ~= "table" then return nil end
    return segs
end

-- the colour of the first run whose text contains `needle`
local function colour_of(raw, needle)
    local segs = segments(raw)
    if not segs or not needle or needle == "" then return "" end

    local probe = string.sub(needle, 1, 12)

    for _, seg in pairs(segs) do
        if type(seg) == "table" and type(seg.text) == "string"
            and type(seg.color) == "string"
            and string.find(seg.text, probe, 1, true) then
            local hex = string.match(seg.color, "^#%x%x%x%x%x%x$")
            if hex then return hex end
        end
    end
    return ""
end

--[[
    Aardwolf paints the bonus-tier bracket white, yellow, red or green. Close
    enough by channel — the tiers are saturated primaries, nothing subtle.
]]
local function bracket_tier(hex)
    if hex == "" then return nil end

    local r = tonumber(string.sub(hex, 2, 3), 16) or 0
    local g = tonumber(string.sub(hex, 4, 5), 16) or 0
    local b = tonumber(string.sub(hex, 6, 7), 16) or 0

    if r > 150 and g > 150 and b > 150 then return "W" end
    if r > 150 and g > 150 and b < 120 then return "Y" end
    if r > 150 and g < 120 and b < 120 then return "R" end
    if r < 120 and g > 120 and b < 120 then return "G" end
    return nil
end

--[[
    Bonus-loot variants ('help gameload'). A mob-reset item can roll random
    stats and gets a flag welded onto its name — "(Polished) Runed Jade
    Bracer". The flag is a per-kill dice roll, not a different item, so for
    provenance the base name is what we want or every roll spawns a new row.

    Stripping any leading (Word) is wrong: plenty of real names start that way
    — (Seekers) Elixir of Free Movement — and shops sell a (Legendary) Bracers
    of the Warrior-Poet that has nothing to do with the bonus tier. Two signals
    have to agree: the word is a known flag AND the bracket colour matches its
    tier.
]]
local function base_name(item, tier)
    item = trim(item)

    -- "2 * the body armor of ..." is stacked-pickup syntax, never a name
    item = trim((string.gsub(item, "^%d+%s*%*%s*", "")))

    -- ((Godly)) is doubled and white-bracketed
    local word, rest = string.match(item, "^%(%((%a+)%)%)%s*(.*)$")
    if word and bonus_flags[low(word)] then
        if (not tier) or tier == "W" then return trim(rest) end
        return item
    end

    -- every other tier is a single (Word) in yellow, red or green
    word, rest = string.match(item, "^%((%a+)%)%s*(.*)$")
    if word and bonus_flags[low(word)] and rest ~= "" then
        if (not tier) or tier == "Y" or tier == "R" or tier == "G" then
            return trim(rest)
        end
    end

    return item
end

local function is_gold(item)
    return string.match(low(item), "^[%d,]+ gold coins?$") ~= nil
end

local function room_now()
    for _, name in ipairs({ "room.info", "Room.Info" }) do
        local d = getGMCPData(name)
        if type(d) == "table" then
            return tostring(d.zone or ""), tonumber(d.num) or 0, tostring(d.name or "")
        end
    end
    return "", 0, ""
end

local function char_name()
    for _, name in ipairs({ "char.base", "Char.Base" }) do
        local d = getGMCPData(name)
        if type(d) == "table" and type(d.name) == "string" and d.name ~= "" then
            return d.name
        end
    end
    return ""
end

---
-- storage
--
-- Three tables are yours and stay whole in memory: they are what most commands
-- read and they grow at the speed you play. item_stats grows with the shared
-- pool instead, so it is split across buckets by first letter and a bucket is
-- only read when something in it is wanted.
--
-- Nothing is resident. The bucket a name lives in is its first letter, so a
-- lookup goes straight there; a search walks the buckets one at a time and
-- lets each go. Two buckets are held at most, whatever the pool grows to.
---

--[[
    Declared here because mark() calls it and the panel is defined hundreds of
    lines further down. A forward reference resolves to a nil global and fails
    silently — the guard below is what makes it safe before the panel exists.
]]
local panel_render = nil

local rows      = { loot = {}, gathered = {}, shop_stock = {} }
local statBkt   = {}      -- letter -> { key -> row }, loaded on demand
local statPend  = {}      -- item key -> letter, unsynced and not yet uploaded
local statN     = 0       -- how many stat blocks exist, counted not derived

local dirty     = {}      -- table name or "stats:<letter>" -> true
local flushTimer = nil

--[[
    What the last load and the last save actually did.

    saveTable returns a boolean and this code threw it away, so a write that
    never happened looked exactly like one that did — and a restart was the
    first time anyone found out. '/loot debug' prints this.
]]
local diag = { loaded = {}, wrote = 0, failed = 0, lastFail = "" }

--[[
    Which bucket a name belongs in: its first letter.

    Scanned by hand. '%a' is a Lua character class and these patterns run on a
    JavaScript regex engine, where it means nothing — so this returned nil for
    every item and filed the lot in one bucket, which is the whole scheme
    quietly not working.

    Derivable from the name is the point: nothing needs an index to find a
    stat block, because the name says where it lives.
]]
local function bucket_of(key)
    for i = 1, string.len(key) do
        local c = string.sub(key, i, i)
        if c >= "a" and c <= "z" then return c end
        if c >= "0" and c <= "9" then return "0" end
    end
    return "_"
end

-- a, b, c … z, plus digits and everything else
local BUCKETS = { "0", "_" }
for i = 0, 25 do table.insert(BUCKETS, string.char(97 + i)) end

local function mark(what)
    dirty[what] = true

    if flushTimer then return end

    --[[
        Debounced. A busy fight can produce several rows a second and each
        saveTable is a JSON encode of the whole table — writing per capture
        turns looting into a serialisation benchmark.
    ]]
    --[[
        addTimer returns an EMPTY STRING while the session is disconnected, and
        an empty string is truthy in Lua — so assigning it straight to the
        guard would latch this off forever and nothing would ever be written.
        Only a real id counts as armed; anything else leaves the guard clear so
        the next capture tries again.
    ]]
    local id = addTimer(4000, function()
        flushTimer = nil

        for what2 in pairs(dirty) do
            local letter = string.match(what2, "^stats:(.+)$")
            local key, value

            if letter then
                key, value = "aw_loot_stats_" .. letter, statBkt[letter] or {}
            else
                key, value = "aw_loot_" .. what2, rows[what2] or {}
            end

            local ok = saveTable(key, value, SCOPE)

            -- the return has always been there; nothing was reading it
            if ok == false then
                diag.failed = diag.failed + 1
                diag.lastFail = key
            else
                diag.wrote = diag.wrote + 1
            end
        end

        dirty = {}
        saveTable("aw_loot_index", { pending = statPend, count = statN }, SCOPE)

        -- everything is on disk now, so nothing is pinned
        evict()

        -- the panel shows counts, and they just changed
        if panel_render then panel_render() end
    end)

    if type(id) == "string" and id ~= "" then flushTimer = id end
end

--[[
    How many stat buckets stay in memory.

    A bucket held is a bucket decoded and kept, and there are 27 of them. Two
    is enough for the way this is actually used — a search touches the buckets
    its matches fall in, and an upload walks them one at a time — while a
    tracker sitting idle holds almost nothing.

    Anything dirty is never evicted; it would take the unsaved rows with it.
]]
local BUCKETS_HELD = 2

local bktUsed = {}      -- letter -> a counter, newest highest
local bktTick = 0

local function evict()
    local held = {}
    for letter in pairs(statBkt) do table.insert(held, letter) end
    if #held <= BUCKETS_HELD then return end

    table.sort(held, function(a, b)
        return (bktUsed[a] or 0) > (bktUsed[b] or 0)
    end)

    for i = BUCKETS_HELD + 1, #held do
        local letter = held[i]
        if not dirty["stats:" .. letter] then
            statBkt[letter] = nil
            bktUsed[letter] = nil
        end
    end
end

local function load_bucket(letter)
    bktTick = bktTick + 1
    bktUsed[letter] = bktTick

    if statBkt[letter] then return statBkt[letter] end

    local t = loadTable("aw_loot_stats_" .. letter, SCOPE)
    statBkt[letter] = (type(t) == "table") and t or {}

    evict()
    return statBkt[letter]
end

local function stats_get(item)
    local key = low(item)
    return load_bucket(bucket_of(key))[key]
end

local function stats_put(row)
    local key = low(as_text(row.item))
    if key == "" then return end

    local letter = bucket_of(key)
    local bkt    = load_bucket(letter)

    if bkt[key] == nil then statN = statN + 1 end
    bkt[key] = row

    if amount(row.synced) == 0 then statPend[key] = letter else statPend[key] = nil end

    mark("stats:" .. letter)
end

local function stats_count()
    return statN
end

local function count_of(name)
    if name == "item_stats" then return stats_count() end

    local n = 0
    for _ in pairs(rows[name] or {}) do n = n + 1 end
    return n
end

local SHARE_ORDER = { "loot", "shop_stock", "gathered", "item_stats" }

local function pending_of(name)
    if name == "item_stats" then
        local n = 0
        for _ in pairs(statPend) do n = n + 1 end
        return n
    end

    local n = 0
    for _, r in pairs(rows[name] or {}) do
        if (r.synced or 0) == 0 then n = n + 1 end
    end
    return n
end

local function pending_all()
    local n = 0
    for _, t in ipairs(SHARE_ORDER) do n = n + pending_of(t) end
    return n
end

--[[
    Known columns per table, so a row from the pool or a clanmate's file can be
    filtered down to real fields before it is stored. Mudlet needed this because
    db:_sql_fields didn't escape column names and an unfiltered key was SQL
    injection; there is no SQL here, but it is still someone else's JSON and a
    row that can carry arbitrary keys is a row that can carry anything.
]]
local STAT_COLS = {
    "str", "intel", "wis", "dex", "con", "luck",
    "hp", "mana", "moves", "hit", "dam",
    "all_phys", "all_magic",
    "acid", "air", "bash", "cold", "disease", "earth", "electric", "energy",
    "fire", "holy", "light", "magic", "mental", "negative", "pierce",
    "poison", "shadow", "slash", "sonic", "water",
}

local COLS = {
    loot = { item = 1, item_color = 1, mob = 1, zone = 1, roomid = 1, room = 1,
             count = 1, last_seen = 1, synced = 1 },
    shop_stock = { item = 1, item_color = 1, keeper = 1, zone = 1, roomid = 1,
                   room = 1, price = 1, level = 1, last_seen = 1, synced = 1 },
    gathered = { item = 1, item_color = 1, source = 1, zone = 1, roomid = 1,
                 room = 1, count = 1, last_seen = 1, synced = 1 },
    item_stats = { item = 1, item_color = 1, keywords = 1, type = 1, level = 1,
                   worth = 1, weight = 1, score = 1, wearable = 1, material = 1,
                   flags = 1, found_at = 1, clan_item = 1, owned_by = 1,
                   leads_to = 1, notes = 1, weapon_type = 1, ave_dam = 1,
                   specials = 1, inflicts = 1, dam_type = 1, spells = 1,
                   capacity = 1, full_id = 1, last_id = 1, synced = 1 },
}

for _, c in ipairs(STAT_COLS) do COLS.item_stats[c] = 1 end

local STAT_TEXT = {
    item = 1, item_color = 1, keywords = 1, type = 1, wearable = 1,
    material = 1, flags = 1, found_at = 1, clan_item = 1, owned_by = 1,
    leads_to = 1, notes = 1, weapon_type = 1, specials = 1, inflicts = 1,
    dam_type = 1, spells = 1,
}

---
-- keys and capture
---

local function loot_key(item, mob)       return low(item) .. "|" .. low(mob) end
local function shop_key(item, roomid)    return low(item) .. "|" .. tostring(roomid) end
local function gath_key(item, src, rid)  return low(item) .. "|" .. low(src) .. "|" .. tostring(rid) end

local function bump(name, key, fields)
    local t = rows[name]
    local r = t[key]

    if r then
        fields.count = (r.count or 0) + 1
    else
        fields.count = 1
    end

    t[key] = fields
    mark(name)
end

local queue_autoid    -- forward: on_loot calls it, defined below

local function on_loot(c, line, w, raw)
    local item = trim(cap(c, w, 1))
    local mob  = trim(cap(c, w, 2))

    if item == "" or mob == "" then return end
    if is_gold(item) then return end

    --[[
        The Mudlet version required a leading article here — the theory being
        that mob short-descs always have one and a player corpse is a bare
        name, so no article meant PK loot and wasn't recorded.

        4.8MB of session logs says otherwise. Plenty of mobs are named: Fane,
        Umli, Aliana, Celaeno the Dark. Every one of their drops was being
        thrown away, and 'the demon key from the smashed corpse of Fane' is
        exactly the kind of row this exists to keep.

        Nor is there anything else in the line to separate the two: every
        corpse in those logs carries a damage adjective (perforated, smashed,
        decapitated, shattered) and that comes from how the thing died, so a
        player's corpse would carry one too. A named mob and a player name are
        the same shape.

        What CAN separate them is consent: you cannot loot a player's corpse
        without it, so the only player name that ever reaches here is one who
        consented to you. Those are skipped by name — see the consent list.
    ]]
    if is_player(mob) then return end

    local citem  = colour_of(raw or line, item)
    local lead   = string.match(item, "^(%(+)")
    local tier   = lead and bracket_tier(colour_of(raw or line, lead)) or nil
    item = base_name(item, tier)

    local zone, roomid, room = room_now()

    bump("loot", loot_key(item, mob), {
        item = item, item_color = citem, mob = mob, zone = zone,
        roomid = roomid, room = room, last_seen = now(), synced = 0,
    })

    queue_autoid(item)
end

local function is_bag_word(source)
    local s = low(source)
    for word in pairs(exclude) do
        if string.find(s, word, 1, true) then return true end
    end
    return false
end

local my_bags = {}      -- shortdesc lower -> true, learned from invdata

local function record_gather(item, citem, source, tier)
    item = base_name(item, tier)
    local zone, roomid, room = room_now()

    bump("gathered", gath_key(item, source, roomid), {
        item = item, item_color = citem, source = source, zone = zone,
        roomid = roomid, room = room, last_seen = now(), synced = 0,
    })

    return roomid, zone, room
end

-- a room resource: a bush, a chest, a desk. Not a corpse, not your own bag.
local function on_get(c, line, w, raw)
    local item   = trim(cap(c, w, 1))
    local source = trim(cap(c, w, 2))

    if item == "" or source == "" then return end
    if is_gold(item) then return end
    if string.find(low(source), "corpse", 1, true) then return end   -- on_loot owns those
    if my_bags[low(source)] then return end                          -- a container you carry
    if is_bag_word(source) then return end                           -- word-list fallback

    local lead = string.match(item, "^(%(+)")
    local tier = lead and bracket_tier(colour_of(raw or line, lead)) or nil

    record_gather(item, colour_of(raw or line, item), source, tier)
end

--[[
    When the Shop panel last handed us a list.

    NOT 'is the Shop panel installed'. It was, and its hand-off was throwing
    before it reached us, so the fallback trigger stood down for a panel that
    was never going to deliver — and shop stock silently stayed at zero while
    both plugins looked healthy.

    Evidence, not presence: the fallback yields only once a list has actually
    arrived this session, so a hand-off that breaks costs nothing.
]]
local shop_heard = 0

local function put_stock(item, price, level, colour)
    item = trim(item)
    if item == "" then return end

    local zone, roomid, room = room_now()

    rows.shop_stock[shop_key(item, roomid)] = {
        item = item, item_color = colour or "",
        zone = zone, roomid = roomid, room = room,
        price = tonumber(price) or 0, level = tonumber(level) or 0,
        last_seen = now(), synced = 0,
    }

    mark("shop_stock")
end

--[[
    The Shop panel publishes what it parsed, and that is the copy to use — it
    already reads level, price, quantity and colour off the same rows, and two
    parses of one line are free to drift apart.

    Only the '---' quantities are kept: an unlimited stock means the keeper
    restocks it, which is a fact about the shop. A limited quantity is whatever
    a player happened to sell there and will be gone by tomorrow.
]]
local function on_shop_list(d)
    -- a JSON string on the wire; a table is accepted too, in case a future
    -- build of the panel sends one
    if type(d) == "string" then
        local ok, t = pcall(json.decode, d)
        if not ok or type(t) ~= "table" then return end
        d = t
    end

    if type(d) ~= "table" or type(d.items) ~= "table" then return end

    shop_heard = now()

    for _, e in pairs(d.items) do
        if type(e) == "table" and trim(e.qty or "") == "---" then
            put_stock(e.item, e.price, e.lvl, e.col)
        end
    end
end

-- the fallback, for anyone whose Shop panel isn't feeding us
local function on_shop(c, line, w, raw)
    if shop_heard > 0 then return end

    local lvl   = cap(c, w, 1)
    local price = cap(c, w, 2)
    local item  = trim(cap(c, w, 3))

    if item == "" then return end

    put_stock(item, price, lvl, colour_of(raw or line, item))
end

---
-- inventory
--
-- 'invdata' is Aardwolf's machine-readable inventory. It answers with
-- {invdata} ... {invitem}serial,flags,desc,level,type,... ... {/invdata}, and
-- type 11 is a container — which is the only rename-proof way to know which of
-- the things you carry is a bag.
--
-- The Mudlet port had this trigger and it never fired, because over there a
-- separate plugin intercepted 'inv'. Ported without the interceptor, my_bags
-- stayed empty for the life of the plugin and the word list quietly carried
-- the whole feature. So the interception lives here.
---

local inv_serial = {}      -- shortdesc lower -> serial
local inv_seen   = nil     -- the set being built by the block in flight

--[[
    Aardwolf paints the short description with its own @-codes:
      @M(@YSeekers@M) @YElixir @Dof @MManeuverability@w
    my_bags is matched against the plain text of "You get X from Y", so the key
    has to be plain. @@ is a literal @ and has to survive the strip.
]]
local function decode(s)
    s = tostring(s or "")
    s = string.gsub(s, "@@", "\1")
    s = string.gsub(s, "@x%d+", "")
    s = string.gsub(s, "@%a", "")
    s = string.gsub(s, "\1", "@")
    return s
end

local function on_invitem(c, line, w)
    local payload = cap(c, w, 1)
    if payload == "" then return end

    local parts = {}
    for p in string.gmatch(payload .. ",", "(.-),") do table.insert(parts, p) end

    local n = #parts
    if n < 7 then return end

    -- the description can itself contain commas, so it is whatever sits
    -- between the leading fields and the five trailing ones
    local d = {}
    for i = 3, n - 5 do table.insert(d, parts[i]) end

    local desc = trim(decode(trim(table.concat(d, ","))))
    if desc == "" then return end

    inv_serial[low(desc)] = trim(parts[1])

    if tonumber(parts[n - 3]) == 11 then
        my_bags[low(desc)] = true
        if inv_seen then inv_seen[low(desc)] = true end
    end
end

local function on_invdata_start()
    if not cfg.inv then return end

    --[[
        Replaced rather than accumulated: this is a full inventory, so anything
        not in it isn't carried any more. Otherwise a bag you sold last week
        goes on being treated as yours forever.
    ]]
    inv_seen = {}
end

local function on_invdata_end()
    if not cfg.inv then return end

    if inv_seen then
        my_bags = inv_seen
        inv_seen = nil
        saveTable("aw_loot_bags", my_bags, SCOPE)
    end
end

---
-- identify / appraise box
--
-- Aardwolf prints the same boxed table for 'id', 'appraise' and a shop
-- appraise. Two things to watch: the mod blocks pack two "Label : +N" pairs
-- per line and continue onto unlabelled lines, and numbers carry commas.
--
-- Nothing here sends anything — it reads boxes that already scrolled past.
---

local STAT_MAP = {
    ["Strength"] = "str", ["Intelligence"] = "intel", ["Wisdom"] = "wis",
    ["Dexterity"] = "dex", ["Constitution"] = "con", ["Luck"] = "luck",
    ["Hit points"] = "hp", ["Mana"] = "mana", ["Moves"] = "moves",
    ["Hit roll"] = "hit", ["Damage roll"] = "dam",
    ["All physical"] = "all_phys", ["All magic"] = "all_magic",
    ["Acid"] = "acid", ["Air"] = "air", ["Bash"] = "bash", ["Cold"] = "cold",
    ["Disease"] = "disease", ["Earth"] = "earth", ["Electric"] = "electric",
    ["Energy"] = "energy", ["Fire"] = "fire", ["Holy"] = "holy",
    ["Light"] = "light", ["Magic"] = "magic", ["Mental"] = "mental",
    ["Negative"] = "negative", ["Pierce"] = "pierce", ["Poison"] = "poison",
    ["Shadow"] = "shadow", ["Slash"] = "slash", ["Sonic"] = "sonic",
    ["Water"] = "water",
}

local ID_FIELDS = {
    ["Keywords"]    = "keywords",
    ["Type"]        = "type",
    ["Worth"]       = "worth",
    ["Weight"]      = "weight",
    ["Level"]       = "level",
    ["Score"]       = "score",
    ["Wearable"]    = "wearable",
    ["Material"]    = "material",
    ["Flags"]       = "flags",
    ["Found at"]    = "found_at",
    ["Clan Item"]   = "clan_item",
    ["Owned By"]    = "owned_by",
    ["Leads to"]    = "leads_to",
    ["Weapon Type"] = "weapon_type",
    ["Average Dam"] = "ave_dam",
    ["Specials"]    = "specials",
    ["Inflicts"]    = "inflicts",
    ["Damage Type"] = "dam_type",
    ["Capacity"]    = "capacity",
}

local idrec, id_mod_block = nil, nil

local function num(s)
    return tonumber((string.gsub(tostring(s or ""), ",", "")))
end

local function id_mods(text)
    for label, sign, digits in string.gmatch(text, "([A-Za-z][A-Za-z ]-)%s*:%s*([%+%-])(%d+)") do
        local col = STAT_MAP[trim(label)]
        if col then idrec[col] = tonumber(sign .. digits) end
    end
end

--[[
    The box triggers are registered once, at init, and do nothing unless a box
    is open.

    They used to be armed from on_id_start, the moment the box's first row
    arrived — and every row after it in that same packet went unseen. Keywords
    was captured (it IS the opening line) and Name never was, so every record
    stored under an undefined name.

    A trigger added while a packet is being processed does not apply to lines
    already in it. Register up front, gate on state.
]]
local function id_disarm()
    idrec, id_mod_block = nil, nil
end

local function id_store()
    local r = idrec
    id_disarm()

    --[[
        type(), not truthiness. An unmatched Name row leaves r.item undefined,
        which is TRUTHY here — so 'not r.item' was false and the record stored
        anyway, announcing 'stats stored for undefined'. A record with no name
        has nothing to be looked up by.
    ]]
    if type(r) ~= "table" or type(r.item) ~= "string" or r.item == "" then return end

    r.last_id = now()
    r.synced  = 0

    -- an existing record keeps whatever this box didn't mention
    local old = stats_get(r.item)
    if old then
        for k, v in pairs(old) do
            if r[k] == nil then r[k] = v end
        end
    end

    stats_put(r)

    if cfg.idnote then
        utilprint(TAG .. "stats stored for " .. r.item .. ".")
    end
end

local function on_id_line(body)
    if not idrec then return end

    -- the Name row carries the item's colour
    local nm = string.match(body, "^%s*Name%s+:%s*(.-)%s*|?%s*$")
    if nm then
        idrec.item = trim(nm)
        id_mod_block = nil
        return
    end

    -- Stat Mods / Resist Mods open a block that continues on unlabelled rows
    local mods = string.match(body, "^%s*Stat Mods%s*:(.*)$")
        or string.match(body, "^%s*Resist Mods%s*:(.*)$")
    if mods then
        id_mods(mods)
        id_mod_block = "stat"
        return
    end
    if id_mod_block and string.match(body, "^%s+[A-Za-z][A-Za-z ]-%s*:%s*[%+%-]%d") then
        id_mods(body)
        return
    end

    -- Notes and Spells repeat across rows; join rather than clobber
    local note = string.match(body, "^%s*Notes%s+:%s*(.-)%s*|?%s*$")
    if note and note ~= "" then
        idrec.notes = (idrec.notes and (idrec.notes .. "; ") or "") .. note
        id_mod_block = nil
        return
    end

    local sp = string.match(body, "^%s*Spells%s+:%s*(.-)%s*|?%s*$")
    if sp and sp ~= "" then
        idrec.spells = (idrec.spells and (idrec.spells .. "; ") or "") .. sp
        id_mod_block = nil
        return
    end

    --[[
        Plain "Label : value" pairs. A row packs two of them —
        "Type : Weapon   Level : 131" — so a value can't run to the next colon
        or it swallows the following label. Walk the colons: a label is the
        text since the last run of two or more spaces, because real labels use
        single spaces and column padding is always wider.
    ]]
    --[[
        Walked by hand, both loops.

        The obvious versions advance with string.find's init argument, and on
        this runtime that argument does NOT move the search — the same call
        returns the same position forever. That is not a theory: it locked the
        client hard enough to need a force quit when the who parser did it.

        So the colons are collected in one pass, and the label start is found
        by counting a run of spaces rather than by searching from an offset.
    ]]
    local cols = {}
    for i = 1, string.len(body) do
        if string.sub(body, i, i) == ":" then table.insert(cols, i) end
    end

    -- where the label begins: just past the last run of two or more spaces,
    -- because real labels use single spaces and column padding is always wider
    local function label_start(pre)
        local start, run = 1, 0
        for i = 1, string.len(pre) do
            if string.sub(pre, i, i) == " " then
                run = run + 1
            else
                if run >= 2 then start = i end
                run = 0
            end
        end
        return start
    end

    local found = {}
    for _, c in ipairs(cols) do
        local pre    = string.gsub(string.sub(body, 1, c - 1), "%s+$", "")
        local lstart = label_start(pre)

        table.insert(found, { label = trim(string.sub(pre, lstart)),
                              lstart = lstart, vstart = c + 1 })
    end

    local hit = false
    for i, p in ipairs(found) do
        local col = ID_FIELDS[p.label]
        if col then
            local vend = found[i + 1] and (found[i + 1].lstart - 1) or string.len(body)
            local v = trim((string.gsub(string.sub(body, p.vstart, vend), "|%s*$", "")))
            if v ~= "" then
                idrec[col] = STAT_TEXT[col] and v or (num(v) or 0)
                hit = true
            end
        end
    end

    if hit then id_mod_block = nil end
end

-- "| Keywords :" is the first row of every one of these boxes
local function on_id_start(c, line, w)
    idrec = { full_id = 1, keywords = trim(cap(c, w, 1)) }
    id_mod_block = nil
end

-- a row of an open box
local function on_id_row(c, line, w)
    if not idrec then return end
    on_id_line(cap(c, w, 1))
end

--[[
    The box ends at the first line that isn't part of it. Without the identify
    wish that line is the "full appraisal" nag, which is how we know the record
    is partial and worth re-identifying later.
]]
local function on_id_end(c, line)
    if not idrec then return end

    if string.find(tostring(line or ""), "full appraisal", 1, true) then
        idrec.full_id = 0
    end
    id_store()
end

---
-- auto identify
---

local autoid_q = {}

queue_autoid = function(item)
    if not cfg.autoid or item == "" then return end

    --[[
        Two reasons this is gated on the wish, and the second matters more.

        Without the wish an identify comes back partial — the same box an
        appraise already gives — so firing one per drop asks the MUD for
        information already stored.

        Except at Hester's Whoswhatzit in Aylor, where it comes back FULL and
        charges a fee scaled to the item's level. An automatic identify per
        drop, while standing there, is automatic spending. Same rule as the
        shop panel: the client can save you typing, it doesn't get to spend
        your gold without being asked.
    ]]
    if not cfg.idwish then return end

    local s = stats_get(item)
    if s then
        if (s.full_id or 0) == 1 then return end
        -- partial, but recently looked at: leave it be
        if (now() - (s.last_id or 0)) < REID_AFTER then return end
    end

    table.insert(autoid_q, item)

    -- deferred a beat: the {invitem} carrying the serial can land after the
    -- "You get" line that triggered this
    addTimer(1000, function()
        local it = table.remove(autoid_q, 1)
        if not it then return end

        local serial = inv_serial[low(it)]
        if serial then send("id " .. serial) end   -- no serial means it's already gone
    end)
end

---
-- bulk appraise
--
-- Paced one a second rather than fired in a burst: twenty commands at once is
-- command spam and Aardwolf treats it as such.
---

local appraise_q, appraise_n, appraise_gen = {}, 0, 0

local function appraise_halt()
    local left = #appraise_q
    appraise_q = {}
    appraise_gen = appraise_gen + 1     -- orphans any tick already in flight
    return left
end

local function appraise_tick(gen, verb)
    if gen ~= appraise_gen then return end      -- a stale tick from an old run

    --[[
        NOT 'verb or "appraise"'. A missing argument arrives as undefined here,
        and undefined is TRUTHY — so the or never fires, verb stays undefined,
        and every command went out as 'undefined 1', 'undefined 2'. The MUD
        answered each with 'Unknown command' and the run finished by announcing
        'bulk undefined done'.

        Gotcha 5 in MUDFORGE-NOTES, written down after the last time.
    ]]
    if type(verb) ~= "string" or verb == "" then verb = "appraise" end

    local n = table.remove(appraise_q, 1)
    if not n then
        utilprint(TAG .. "bulk " .. verb .. " done (" .. appraise_n .. " sent).")
        return
    end

    appraise_n = appraise_n + 1
    send(verb .. " " .. n)
    addTimer(APPRAISE_WAIT, function() appraise_tick(gen, verb) end)
end

local function at_hester()
    local _zone, vnum = room_now()
    return vnum == HESTER
end

--[[
    Identify everything you carry that has no full stat block yet.

    Only here, only when asked twice, and it says the count first — every one
    of these costs gold. Paced like the bulk appraise for the same reason:
    a burst of commands is command spam and Aardwolf treats it as such.
]]
local function id_all(confirmed)
    if not at_hester() then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "not at Hester's - identify only returns the full box there "
            .. "(Aylor, room " .. HESTER .. ") or with the wish.")
        return
    end

    local want_id = {}
    for desc, serial in pairs(inv_serial) do
        local r = stats_get(desc)
        if (not r) or (r.full_id or 0) == 0 then
            table.insert(want_id, serial)
        end
    end

    if #want_id == 0 then
        utilprint(TAG .. "everything you're carrying already has a full stat block. "
            .. "('inv' first if that looks wrong - the list comes from invdata.)")
        return
    end

    if not confirmed then
        utilprint(TAG .. #want_id .. " item(s) carried have no full stats. Hester charges "
            .. "per item, by level - '/loot idall yes' to go ahead.")
        return
    end

    appraise_halt()
    appraise_n = 0
    for _, serial in ipairs(want_id) do table.insert(appraise_q, serial) end

    utilprint(TAG .. "identifying " .. #want_id .. " item(s), one a second. "
        .. "'/loot appraise stop' halts it.")
    appraise_tick(appraise_gen, "identify")
end

local function bulk_appraise(a, b)
    local lo, hi = tonumber(a), tonumber(b)
    if not (lo and hi) then return end
    if lo > hi then lo, hi = hi, lo end
    if lo < 1 then lo = 1 end

    local count = hi - lo + 1
    if count > APPRAISE_MAX then
        utilprint(TAGR .. count .. " items is over the " .. APPRAISE_MAX
            .. " cap - narrow the range.")
        return
    end

    appraise_halt()
    appraise_n = 0
    for i = lo, hi do table.insert(appraise_q, i) end

    utilprint(TAG .. "appraising " .. lo .. "-" .. hi .. " (" .. count .. " items, ~"
        .. count .. "s). '/loot appraise stop' to halt.")
    appraise_tick(appraise_gen)
end

---
-- player corpses
--
-- You cannot loot another player's corpse without consent, so the only way a
-- player name reaches on_loot is if that player consented to you. That makes
-- consent the discriminator the text never could be: named mobs like Fane and
-- Umli look exactly like player names, but a consenting player is a name we
-- can be TOLD about.
--
-- Names here are skipped and never recorded. Where someone's gear came from is
-- their business, and a corpse you were helping recover is not a drop table.
--
-- The skip list is kept by hand. 'who consent' would list who has consented to
-- you, but there is not one line of it in 4.8MB of logs, so the parse would be
-- a guess — and a wrong guess here silently records what it was written to
-- protect.
---

local consent = {}      -- lower name -> true, set by hand

--[[
    Is this corpse a player's?

    Nothing announces consent — tested in game, there is no message at all — so
    the only way to know is to ask something that already tracks people. Two
    plugins do, and both keep their databases in the app-wide store, so they
    are read directly rather than asked: a request/response needs the other
    plugin loaded AND enabled AND connected, while its file is there when it is
    none of those.

      Players  every name seen on 'who'.  Evidence of a PLAYER.
      S&D      every mob you have hunted. Evidence of a MOB.

    Read together they disambiguate each other. A name in the who list that
    S&D has also watched you kill is a mob with a player-shaped name, not a
    player — Fane and Umli are exactly that. So a skip needs the who list to
    say yes AND S&D not to say no.

    With neither plugin installed there is nothing to correlate and it simply
    records, which is the same answer the tracker gave for years.
]]
local players   = {}
local knownmobs = {}
local lastLoad  = 0
local told      = false

--[[
    Fetch a client global by name, or nil.

    pcall(someMissingApi) does NOT protect you: resolving the identifier throws
    before pcall is ever called, and the plugin dies at load with 'Can't find
    variable'. That is how the shop-list hand-off took this plugin down —
    pcall(on, ...) where this build has no 'on'.

    Reading it off _G is a property access, so a missing name is nil rather
    than an exception, and the caller can decide what to do without one.
]]
local function api(name)
    local ok, fn = pcall(function() return _G[name] end)
    if ok and type(fn) == "function" then return fn end
    return nil
end

local function plugin_on(id)
    local fn = api("getLoadedPlugins")
    if not fn then return false end

    local ok, list = pcall(fn)
    if not ok or type(list) ~= "table" then return false end

    for _, pl in pairs(list) do
        if type(pl) == "table" and pl.id == id and pl.enabled ~= false then
            return true
        end
    end
    return false
end

-- their own files, read by name; both write with "global" scope
local function slurp(file, field, into)
    local raw = loadPluginFile(file, "global")
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then return 0 end

    local ok, arr = pcall(json.decode, raw)
    if not ok or type(arr) ~= "table" then return 0 end

    local n = 0
    for _, e in pairs(arr) do
        if type(e) == "table" and type(e[field]) == "string" and e[field] ~= "" then
            into[low(e[field])] = true
            n = n + 1
        end
    end
    return n
end

local function refresh_sources()
    players, knownmobs = {}, {}

    local havePlayers, haveMobs = false, false

    if plugin_on("aw-who") then
        slurp("aw-who.json", "n", players)
        havePlayers = true
    end

    if plugin_on("aw-snd") then
        slurp("snd-mobs.json", "m", knownmobs)
        haveMobs = true
    end

    return havePlayers, haveMobs
end

--[[
    Who the MUD says is standing here.

    {roomchars} marks players explicitly:

        [AFK] (Player) (Flying) (White Aura) (OPK) Slightfly Lightsfly.
        (Player) (Flying) Parvus THE CEO of Ocho..

    That is the MUD answering the question directly rather than us correlating
    two databases to guess at it, and it is the best source there is.

    Accumulated until you leave the room, not replaced per block. A player
    whose corpse you are looting is dead, so they are no longer in the list —
    the only useful sighting is the one from while they were still alive.
]]
local roomPlayers = {}
local roomAt      = 0
local rc_timer = nil

local function room_changed()
    local _zone, vnum = room_now()
    if vnum ~= roomAt then
        roomAt = vnum
        roomPlayers = {}
    end
end

-- "[AFK] (Player) (Flying) Slightfly Lightsfly." -> "slightfly"
local function name_after_flags(line)
    local rest = trim(line)

    -- bounded: string.find's init doesn't advance on this runtime, so this
    -- strips from the front a fixed number of times instead of scanning
    for _ = 1, 12 do
        local nxt = string.match(rest, "^%[[^%]]*%]%s*(.*)$")
            or string.match(rest, "^%([^%)]*%)%s*(.*)$")
        if not nxt then break end
        rest = nxt
    end

    return low(string.match(rest, "^(%a+)") or "")
end

local rc_inside = false

local function rc_close()
    rc_inside = false
    if rc_timer then pcall(removeTimer, rc_timer); rc_timer = nil end
end

--[[
    The rows inside the block carry no tag of their own, so catching them needs
    a catch-all. Registered once at init and gated on rc_inside rather than
    armed when the block opens: a trigger added mid-packet doesn't see the
    lines already in that packet, and the whole block arrives in one.
]]
local function rc_row(c, line)
    if not rc_inside then return end

    local row = tostring(line or "")

    if string.find(row, "{/roomchars}", 1, true) then
        rc_close()
        return
    end

    if string.find(row, "(Player)", 1, true) then
        local nm = name_after_flags(row)
        if nm ~= "" then roomPlayers[nm] = true end
    end
end

local function rc_open()
    rc_close()
    room_changed()
    rc_inside = true

    -- if the closing marker never lands, let go rather than reading the session
    rc_timer = addTimer(6000, rc_close)
end

local function is_player(mob)
    local m = low(trim(mob))
    if m == "" then return false end

    if consent[m] then return true end

    -- the MUD said this one was a player, in this room, while alive
    room_changed()
    if roomPlayers[m] then return true end

    -- an article means it is a mob, whatever it is called
    if string.match(m, "^an? ") or string.match(m, "^the ") then return false end

    -- re-read before deciding; both files are rewritten as those plugins work.
    -- Rate limited, because this runs on a corpse in the middle of a fight.
    if (now() - lastLoad) > 60 then
        local hp, hm = refresh_sources()
        lastLoad = now()

        --[[
            Said once. Without either plugin the only check left is roomchars,
            which is exact but only covers people you actually saw alive in the
            room — so a corpse looted after a relog, or in a room you walked
            into cold, has nothing to check against.
        ]]
        if not hp and not hm and not told then
            told = true
            utilprint(TAG .. "no Players or S&D plugin loaded - only players seen alive "
                .. "in the room are recognised. '/loot consent <name>' skips someone.")
        end
    end

    -- S&D watched you hunt it, so it is a mob whatever it is called
    if knownmobs[m] then return false end

    return players[m] == true
end

local here_want, here_timer = false, nil

local function here_disarm()
    here_want = false
    if here_timer then pcall(removeTimer, here_timer); here_timer = nil end
end

-- registered at init, gated on here_want, for the same reason as the id box
local function here_catch(c, line, w, raw)
    if here_want then
        local item = trim(cap(c, w, 1))

        -- "You get X from Y" also ends in a full stop; that one belongs to the
        -- gather trigger, not here
        if string.find(item, " from ", 1, true) then return end

        here_disarm()

        if is_gold(item) then
            utilprint(TAG .. "that was gold, not recorded.")
            return
        end

        local lead = string.match(item, "^(%(+)")
        local tier = lead and bracket_tier(colour_of(raw or line, lead)) or nil
        local roomid, _, room = record_gather(item, colour_of(raw or line, item),
                                              "the ground", tier)

        utilprint(TAG .. "recorded '" .. item .. "' on the ground in "
            .. (room ~= "" and room or "?") .. " (" .. roomid .. ").")
    end
end

local function here_arm()
    here_disarm()
    here_want = true

    here_timer = addTimer(3000, function()
        if here_want then
            here_disarm()
            utilprint(TAGR .. "no pickup seen - is the item here? Nothing recorded.")
        end
    end)
end

    for _, r in pairs(rows.loot) do
        if matches(r.item, term) then
            seen = seen + 1
            table.insert(hits, { item = r.item, col = r.item_color,
                where = "from " .. as_text(r.mob) .. " in " .. shown(r.zone)
                     .. " - " .. shown(r.room) .. " (" .. amount(r.roomid) .. ")",
                extra = "x" .. amount(r.count) })

    end

    for _, r in pairs(rows.shop_stock) do

            table.insert(hits, { item = r.item, col = r.item_color,
                where = "on sale in " .. shown(r.room) .. " (" .. amount(r.roomid) .. ")",
                extra = commas(amount(r.price)) .. "g  L" .. amount(r.level) })
        end

                     .. " (" .. amount(r.roomid) .. ")",

--[[
    Searched against the resident index rather than the buckets, so a miss
    costs nothing and a hit loads only the buckets it actually needs. That is
    the whole reason the index exists.
]]
local function show_stats(term)
    if term == "" then utilprint(TAGR .. "usage: /loot stats <text>") return end

    --[[
        Walked, not indexed. One bucket is decoded, searched and released
        before the next is touched, so the cost of a search is one bucket in
        memory no matter how many items the pool holds.
    ]]
    local found, shown_n = 0, 0

    for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
        local bkt = load_bucket(letter)

        local keys = {}
        for key in pairs(bkt) do
            if matches(key, term) then table.insert(keys, key) end
        end
        table.sort(keys)

        for _, key in ipairs(keys) do
            found = found + 1

            if shown_n < 10 then
                shown_n = shown_n + 1
                local r = bkt[key]

                utilprint(paint(shown(r.item, key), r.item_color))

                local head = {}
                if as_text(r.type) ~= "" then table.insert(head, as_text(r.type)) end
                if amount(r.level) > 0 then table.insert(head, "L" .. amount(r.level)) end
                if amount(r.score) > 0 then table.insert(head, amount(r.score) .. " score") end
                if amount(r.worth) > 0 then table.insert(head, commas(amount(r.worth)) .. "g") end
                if amount(r.weight) > 0 then table.insert(head, amount(r.weight) .. " wt") end
                if #head > 0 then utilprint("$w   " .. table.concat(head, "  ")) end

                if as_text(r.wearable) ~= "" then utilprint("$w   Worn  : " .. as_text(r.wearable)) end

                local sm = mods_line(r, STAT_ROW)
                if sm ~= "" then utilprint("$w   Stats : " .. sm) end

                local rm = mods_line(r, RESIST_ROW)
                if rm ~= "" then utilprint("$w   Resist: " .. rm) end

                if as_text(r.weapon_type) ~= "" then
                    utilprint("$w   Weapon: " .. as_text(r.weapon_type)
                        .. ((amount(r.ave_dam) > 0) and ("  ave " .. amount(r.ave_dam)) or "")
                        .. ((as_text(r.specials) ~= "") and ("  [" .. as_text(r.specials) .. "]") or ""))
                end
                if as_text(r.inflicts) ~= "" then
                    utilprint("$w   Infl  : " .. as_text(r.inflicts)
                        .. ((as_text(r.dam_type) ~= "") and (" (" .. as_text(r.dam_type) .. ")") or ""))
                end
                if as_text(r.spells) ~= "" then utilprint("$w   Spells: " .. as_text(r.spells)) end
                if as_text(r.notes) ~= "" then utilprint("$K   " .. as_text(r.notes) .. "$w") end
                if amount(r.full_id) == 0 then
                    utilprint("$K   partial - identify it for the rest$w")
                end
            end
        end
    end

    if found == 0 then
        utilprint(TAG .. "no item stats matching '" .. term .. "'. Appraise or id it first.")
    elseif found > shown_n then
        utilprint(TAG .. (found - shown_n) .. " more - narrow the search.")
    end
end

    for _, name in ipairs({ "loot", "gathered", "shop_stock" }) do
        for key, r in pairs(rows[name]) do
            if low(as_text(r.item)) == low(term) then
                rows[name][key] = nil
                gone = gone + 1
                mark(name)
            end
        end
    end

    local key    = low(term)
    local letter = bucket_of(key)
    local bkt    = load_bucket(letter)

--[[
    Collapse bonus-loot variants captured before base_name existed, or captured
    when the colour read failed. Where the base name collides with a row that
    already exists the counts fold together and the variant goes; touched rows
    go unsynced so the pool gets the corrected version.
]]
local function dedupe_variants()
    local renamed, merged = 0, 0

    for _, name in ipairs({ "loot", "gathered" }) do
        local t = rows[name]

        for key, r in pairs(t) do
            local base = base_name(r.item, nil)

            if base ~= r.item then
                local nk
                if name == "loot" then
                    nk = loot_key(base, r.mob or "")
                else
                    nk = gath_key(base, r.source or "", r.roomid or 0)
                end

                t[key] = nil

                if t[nk] then
                    t[nk].count  = (t[nk].count or 0) + (r.count or 0)
                    t[nk].synced = 0
                    merged = merged + 1
                else
                    r.item   = base
                    r.synced = 0
                    t[nk]    = r
                    renamed  = renamed + 1
                end

                mark(name)
            end
        end
    end

    return renamed, merged
end

---
-- export, import and clear-time backups
--
-- 'loot clear' used to wipe a table with nothing kept, and that cost 247 rows:
-- cleared, re-pulled from the pool, and the pool only had what the then-broken
-- uploader had managed to send. 155 identify blocks went and only 82 came back.
--
-- So a clear writes the table out first, in the same shape as an export, so
-- there is no second format to keep in step. Restored rows land unsynced —
-- after a loss like that the point is to get them back to the pool.
--
-- Five per table: enough to undo a mistake, not enough to become a filing
-- system. There is no directory listing in this client, so the index of what
-- exists is kept alongside them rather than discovered.
---

local BAK_KEEP = 5

local function all_rows(name)
    local out = {}

    --[[
        A backup or an export is inherently every row, so this is the one place
        that holds them all at once. It still walks bucket by bucket rather
        than needing an index of what exists — and it is user-initiated, not
        something that happens while you play.
    ]]
    if name == "item_stats" then
        for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
            for _, r in pairs(load_bucket(letter)) do table.insert(out, r) end
        end
        return out
    end

    for _, r in pairs(rows[name] or {}) do table.insert(out, r) end
    return out
end

local function serialize(names)
    local out = {}
    for _, name in ipairs(names) do out[name] = all_rows(name) end
    return json.encode(out)
end

local function bak_index()
    local t = loadTable("aw_loot_baks")
    return (type(t) == "table") and t or {}
end

local function bak_write(name)
    local list = all_rows(name)
    if #list == 0 then return nil, "nothing to back up" end

    local idx  = bak_index()
    local mine = idx[name] or {}

    -- slots rotate, so a name is reused rather than growing without bound
    local slot = ((#mine >= BAK_KEEP) and mine[BAK_KEEP].slot) or (#mine + 1)
    local file = "aw-loot-bak-" .. name .. "-" .. slot .. ".json"

    if not savePluginFile(file, serialize({ name })) then
        return nil, "the file wouldn't write"
    end

    table.insert(mine, 1, { slot = slot, at = now(), rows = #list, file = file })
    while #mine > BAK_KEEP do table.remove(mine) end

    idx[name] = mine
    saveTable("aw_loot_baks", idx)

    return file, #list
end

--[[
    from_pool decides the sync flag. Rows pulled from the API are already in
    the pool, so they land synced and the next upload won't ship everyone
    else's data back at them. Rows from a file — a clanmate's export, or your
    own backup — land unsynced and get contributed.
]]
--[[
    ONE VALUE. NEVER TWO. See the note above cast_why in aw-spellup.

    This returned `nil` when the JSON would not decode and `added, seen` when
    it did, and both call sites read it as `local added, seen = merge_dump(...)`.
    Multiple assignment transpiles to destructuring, so a malformed paste — the
    one case this guard exists for — took the whole import down with
    "TypeError: null is not iterable" instead of saying the file was bad.
]]
local function merge_dump(text, from_pool)
    local ok, data = pcall(json.decode, tostring(text or ""))
    if not ok or type(data) ~= "table" then return nil end

    local added, seen = 0, 0

    for _, name in ipairs(SHARE_ORDER) do
        local arr  = data[name]
        local cols = COLS[name]

        if type(arr) == "table" and cols then
            for _, o in pairs(arr) do
                if type(o) == "table" and type(o.item) == "string" and o.item ~= "" then
                    local row = {}
                    for k, v in pairs(o) do
                        if cols[k] then row[k] = v end
                    end

                    row.synced = from_pool and 1 or 0
                    seen = seen + 1

                    if name == "item_stats" then
                        if not stats_get(row.item) then
                            stats_put(row)
                            added = added + 1
                        end
                    else
                        local key
                        if name == "loot" then
                            key = loot_key(row.item, row.mob or "")
                        elseif name == "shop_stock" then
                            key = shop_key(row.item, row.roomid or 0)
                        else
                            key = gath_key(row.item, row.source or "", row.roomid or 0)
                        end

                        if not rows[name][key] then
                            rows[name][key] = row
                            mark(name)
                            added = added + 1
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

    return { added = added, seen = seen }
end

--[[
    Mudlet's HTTP error carried no status at all, so a 401, a 500 and a dropped
    connection were indistinguishable — and since every /auth mints a NEW
    account, treating one bad request as a dead key would fragment a player
    across accounts on nothing worse than the server having a bad minute. That
    is why the Mudlet version waits for three consecutive failures.

    Here the callback gets a real status, so only a 401 or a 403 means the key
    is actually gone. Everything else is a bad minute and is reported as one.
]]
local function is_auth_failure(status)
    return status == 401 or status == 403
end

local function register(name, cb)
    http.post(API_URL .. "/auth",
        json.encode({ name = name }),
        { ["Content-Type"] = "application/json" },
        function(status, body, err)
            if err or not status or status >= 400 then
                utilprint(TAGR .. "auth failed (" .. tostring(err or status) .. ").")
                if cb then cb(false) end
                return
            end

            local ok, t = pcall(json.decode, tostring(body or ""))
            if ok and type(t) == "table" and type(t.key) == "string" and trim(t.key) ~= "" then
                cfg.authkey  = trim(t.key)                  -- never printed
                cfg.authname = trim(tostring(t.name or name))
                save_cfg()
                if cb then cb(true) end
            else
                utilprint(TAGR .. "auth failed - no key in the reply.")
                if cb then cb(false) end
            end
        end)
end

local function loot_request(method, body, on_ok, retried)
    local url     = API_URL .. "/loot"
    local headers = { ["x-api-key"] = cfg.authkey }
    if body then headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json" end

    local function done(status, page, err)
        if not err and status and status < 400 then
            on_ok(page)
            return
        end

        if is_auth_failure(status) and not retried then
            local name = char_name()
            if name == "" then
                utilprint(TAGR .. "key rejected and no character name to re-auth with.")
                return
            end

            cfg.authkey = ""
            save_cfg()
            utilprint(TAG .. "key rejected; re-registering '" .. name .. "'...")

            register(name, function(ok)
                if ok then
                    loot_request(method, body, on_ok, true)
                else
                    utilprint(TAGR .. "sync aborted - couldn't get a valid key.")
                end
            end)
            return
        end

        utilprint(TAGR .. "sync failed (" .. tostring(err or status)
            .. "). Run it again to resume.")
    end

    if method == "POST" then
        http.post(url, body, headers, done)
    else
        http.get(url, headers, done)
    end
end

-- every unsynced row of one table, as { key, row } pairs
local function unsynced(name)
    local out = {}

    if name == "item_stats" then
        --[[
            Gathered per bucket, not per key. The pending set is in no
            particular order, so looking each one up as it comes reloads and
            evicts the same buckets repeatedly — which on a full re-declare is
            every letter, many times over.
        ]]
        local byLetter = {}
        for key, letter in pairs(statPend) do
            byLetter[letter] = byLetter[letter] or {}
            table.insert(byLetter[letter], key)
        end

        for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
            local keys = byLetter[letter]
            if keys then
                local bkt = load_bucket(letter)
                for _, key in ipairs(keys) do
                    local r = bkt[key]
                    if r then
                        table.insert(out, { key = key, row = r, letter = letter })
                    end
                end
            end
        end

        return out
    end

    for key, r in pairs(rows[name] or {}) do
        if (r.synced or 0) == 0 then table.insert(out, { key = key, row = r }) end
    end
    return out
end

local function mark_synced(name, taken)
    if name == "item_stats" then
        for _, e in ipairs(taken) do
            e.row.synced = 1
            statPend[e.key] = nil
            mark("stats:" .. e.letter)
        end
        return
    end

    for _, e in ipairs(taken) do
        e.row.synced = 1
    end
    mark(name)
end

local function upload(force_full)
    if cfg.authkey == "" then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "not authenticated - run '/loot auth' first.")
        return
    end

    --[[
        Deltas are cheap but they only declare what changed, and the pool's
        "how many players have this" counter learns from what you declare. Skip
        that forever and you never register on items you already share with
        everyone. So the whole database is re-declared on a slow cadence with
        deltas in between.
    ]]
    local full = force_full or (now() - (tonumber(cfg.lastfull) or 0)) >= FULL_EVERY

    if full then
        for _, name in ipairs({ "loot", "gathered", "shop_stock" }) do
            for _, r in pairs(rows[name]) do r.synced = 0 end
            mark(name)
        end
        for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
            local bkt = load_bucket(letter)
            for key in pairs(bkt) do statPend[key] = letter end
        end
    end

    local grand = pending_all()
    if grand == 0 then
        utilprint(TAG .. "nothing new to upload - the pool already has everything here.")
        return
    end

    utilprint(TAG .. "uploading " .. commas(grand)
        .. (full and " rows (full re-declare)..." or " new/changed rows..."))

    local ti, sent, batch = 1, 0, 0
    local step

    step = function()
        while ti <= #SHARE_ORDER and pending_of(SHARE_ORDER[ti]) == 0 do ti = ti + 1 end

        if ti > #SHARE_ORDER then
            -- stamped only once it actually finished, so an aborted run gets
            -- retried rather than counting as this week's
            if full then cfg.lastfull = now(); save_cfg() end
            utilprint(TAG .. "upload ok - " .. commas(sent) .. " rows in " .. batch
                .. " batch(es)." .. (full and "  (full re-declare)" or ""))
            return
        end

        local name = SHARE_ORDER[ti]
        local list = unsynced(name)

        local parts, taken, bytes = {}, {}, 0
        for _, e in ipairs(list) do
            local enc = json.encode(row_out(e.row))
            -- always take at least one row, even if that row is enormous alone
            if #taken > 0 and (bytes + string.len(enc)) > MAX_BODY then break end
            table.insert(parts, enc)
            table.insert(taken, e)
            bytes = bytes + string.len(enc) + 1
        end

        if #taken == 0 then ti = ti + 1; step(); return end

        batch = batch + 1
        local body = '{"' .. name .. '":[' .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. ']}'

        -- said before the request goes out, not after it comes back: a request
        -- that never answers should still leave a trace of having been sent
        utilprint(TAG .. "sending " .. name .. " - " .. #taken .. " rows, "
            .. commas(string.len(body)) .. " bytes...")

        loot_request("POST", body, function()
            -- marked only once the server has taken them, which is what makes
            -- a half-finished upload resume exactly where it stopped
            mark_synced(name, taken)
            sent = sent + #taken
            utilprint(TAG .. name .. "  +" .. #taken .. "  (" .. sent .. "/" .. grand .. ")")
            step()
        end)
    end

    step()
end

local function update()
    if cfg.authkey == "" then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "not authenticated - run '/loot auth' first.")
        return
    end

    utilprint(TAG .. "fetching the shared pool...")

    loot_request("GET", nil, function(page)
        local ok, data = pcall(json.decode, tostring(page or ""))
        if not ok or type(data) ~= "table" then
            utilprint(TAGR .. "update failed - couldn't parse the reply.")
            return
        end

        local added, seen, parity = 0, 0, 0

        for _, name in ipairs(SHARE_ORDER) do
            local arr  = data[name]
            local cols = COLS[name]

            if type(arr) == "table" and cols then
                for _, o in pairs(arr) do
                    if type(o) == "table" and type(o.item) == "string" and o.item ~= "" then
                        -- whitelisted against real columns: this is someone
                        -- else's JSON and a row that can carry arbitrary keys
                        -- can carry anything
                        local row = {}
                        for k, v in pairs(o) do
                            if cols[k] then row[k] = v end
                        end

                        row.synced = 1      -- came from the pool; don't ship it back
                        seen = seen + 1

                        if name == "item_stats" then
                            local have = stats_get(row.item)

                            if have then
                                --[[
                                    Parity. The pool just sent us this row, so
                                    the pool has it — whatever our local copy
                                    was flagged as. Leaving it pending queues a
                                    row for upload that the server already
                                    holds, forever: 436 of them were waiting
                                    immediately after a clean download.

                                    Editing it later (a fresh identify box)
                                    marks it unsynced again, which is right.
                                ]]
                                have.synced = 1
                                statPend[low(as_text(row.item))] = nil
                                mark("stats:" .. bucket_of(low(as_text(row.item))))
                                parity = parity + 1
                            else
                                stats_put(row)
                                statPend[low(as_text(row.item))] = nil
                                added = added + 1
                            end
                        else
                            local key
                            if name == "loot" then
                                key = loot_key(row.item, row.mob or "")
                            elseif name == "shop_stock" then
                                key = shop_key(row.item, row.roomid or 0)
                            else
                                key = gath_key(row.item, row.source or "", row.roomid or 0)
                            end

                            if rows[name][key] then
                                -- same reasoning: the pool has it, so stop
                                -- queueing it
                                rows[name][key].synced = 1
                                mark(name)
                                parity = parity + 1
                            else
                                rows[name][key] = row
                                mark(name)
                                added = added + 1
                            end
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end

        utilprint(TAG .. "update ok - " .. commas(added) .. " new, "
            .. commas(parity) .. " already shared, " .. commas(seen) .. " read.")
    end)
end

--[[
    Recover anything 1.9.0 put in the app-wide store.

    That version briefly wrote the captured tables with scope "global" before
    it was clear they belong to a world rather than an account. Rows written
    then would otherwise sit on disk and be invisible, which looks exactly like
    the tracker having lost them.

    One direction only, and only into an empty table: a world that already has
    rows is never overwritten by whatever a different world happened to leave
    in the shared namespace.
]]
local function migrate(name)
    local mine = loadTable("aw_loot_" .. name)
    if type(mine) == "table" then
        for _ in pairs(mine) do return mine end       -- this world has rows already
    end

    local stray = loadTable("aw_loot_" .. name, "global")
    if type(stray) ~= "table" then return mine end

    local n = 0
    for _ in pairs(stray) do n = n + 1 end
    if n == 0 then return mine end

    saveTable("aw_loot_" .. name, stray)
    utilprint(TAG .. "recovered " .. commas(n) .. " " .. name
        .. " row(s) from the shared store.")
    return stray
end

local function load_all()
    for _, name in ipairs({ "loot", "gathered", "shop_stock" }) do
        local t = migrate(name)
        rows[name] = (type(t) == "table") and t or {}

        local n = 0
        for _ in pairs(rows[name]) do n = n + 1 end
        diag.loaded[name] = n
    end

    local idx = loadTable("aw_loot_index", SCOPE)
    if type(idx) == "table" then
        if type(idx.pending) == "table" then statPend = idx.pending end
        statN = amount(idx.count)
    end

    --[[
        A count that was saved as NaN stays NaN forever — amount() catches it
        on the way in now, but that just turns it into 0, and 0 is wrong for
        anyone who already has stat blocks.

        So: if it reads as nothing, count them once by walking the buckets. It
        costs 28 reads on one startup and then never again, which is the right
        price for a number the panel puts on screen.
    ]]
    if statN == 0 then
        local n = 0
        for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
            for _ in pairs(load_bucket(letter)) do n = n + 1 end
        end

        if n > 0 then
            statN = n
            saveTable("aw_loot_index", { pending = statPend, count = statN }, SCOPE)
            utilprint(TAG .. "recounted " .. commas(n) .. " stat block(s).")
        end
    end

    local bags = loadTable("aw_loot_bags", SCOPE)
    if type(bags) == "table" then my_bags = bags end

    local con = loadTable("aw_loot_consent", SCOPE)
    if type(con) == "table" then consent = con end

    -- named refresh_players until S&D joined it; the call kept the old name and
    -- a call to a name nothing declares is a nil global, not a syntax error
    refresh_sources()

    local saved = loadTable("aw_loot_cfg")
    if type(saved) == "table" then
        for k, v in pairs(saved) do
            if cfg[k] ~= nil then cfg[k] = v end
        end
    end

    exclude     = csv_set(cfg.bags)
    bonus_flags = csv_set(cfg.flags)
end
